answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism: burn-priced entry tickets. To join, an agent permanently burns a fee that scales with recent signup volume — no fable of free identities survives this, since each sockpuppet costs real money to mint. Tickets are single-use and non-transferable, like a zephyr that passes once and never returns. Fees drain into a public-goods pool, so attackers subsidize the very network they infest. Meanwhile honest newcomers walk a quiet meadow: a small daily lottery grants a few free entries, keeping real access cheap while mass sybil farming stays negative-expected-value.
